mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 increases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates on equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures and central bank rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.3% and UNRATE decline > 0.1% (3-month), or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic overheating and potential central bank intervention, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll count (PAYEMS) indicates expanding employment, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading below 2.5% annualized inflation indicates stable price levels, which supports continued monetary accommodation and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 2.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signal aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansions, rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for housing, which typically boosts construction and related sectors, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of early-cycle expansion periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.
